claim: An SDT Type-2 decomposition of LLM confidence separates discrimination from calibration level and reveals unequal-variance structure invisible to ECE.
stance_target: F: measurement-instrument framing of calibration is already occupied for factual QA
scope_conditions: Four 7-9B open-weight models, TriviaQA and Natural Questions, factual QA only
quoted_support: Standard evaluation of LLM confidence relies on calibration metrics (ECE, Brier score) that conflate two distinct capacities: how much a model knows (Type-1 accuracy) and how well its confidence signal tracks that knowledge (Type-2 metacognitive sensitivity).

claim: v3 retracts earlier cross-model efficiency findings because the automated correctness scorer was length-biased; label validity changed the conclusion.
stance_target: Label validation is load-bearing for calibration claims
scope_conditions: Factual QA, exact-match plus similarity scorer
quoted_support: Validated against 1,200 human adjudications, the scorer missed 53% of one model's human-correct answers and 26% of another's

claim: meta-I_2r (mutual information of correctness and discretised confidence over H(correct)) is a model-free efficiency measure, bias-corrected via permutation null with bootstrap CIs.
quoted_support: meta-I_2r is 0 when confidence is uninformative about correctness and approaches its ceiling when confidence fully resolves the correct/incorrect distinction.
